jobs.title: Assistant Professor, Open Specialization with Latin Proficiency
jobs.description: Employment Opportunities About Menu Mission & Vision Catholicity Catholicity Overview Sacred Liturgy Eastern Churches Sacred Music Spiritual Formation Chaplaincy Schedule College News Explore Our Campus Our Home, Lander, WY Faculty & Staff College Leadership Board & Advisory Council Employment Academic Calendar WCC Webstore Return to Overview Open Job Postings Assistant Professor, Open Specialization with Latin Proficiency Wyoming Catholic College invites applications for a full-time faculty position beginning in the 2027-28 academic year. Candidates from any discipline represented in the College’s curriculum may apply. In addition to teaching within his or her own discipline, the successful candidate will teach introductory Latin and therefore must be conversationally proficient in Latin. Latin is the only foreign language taught at Wyoming Catholic College. The College requires all underclassmen to complete two years of coursework in the language, followed by two semesters of guided practice in reading in the junior and senior years. Our goal is to enable all students to receive the Catholic and Western intellectual tradition by reading Latin texts of all types and periods. We seek a colleague whose interests and abilities harmonize with this purpose. About the College: Founded in 2005, Wyoming Catholic College is a private, four-year, Roman Catholic Liberal Arts college located in Lander, Wyoming. It is Wyoming’s first private, four-year undergraduate institution and is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. The College exists to exemplify and promote education of the whole person in three aspects: body, mind, and spirit, and it strives to form virtuous and imaginative generalists. All students take a determinate, integrated curriculum which is firmly rooted in the Catholic faith and the Western tradition, based on the Great Books, and leads to the Bachelor of Arts in Liberal Arts. About the Latin Program: The founding principle of the WCC Latin Program is the often-sidelined truth that Latin is fully a language, valuable because practical competency in Latin makes possible direct access to much of the seminal thought and literary art of Western Civilization and the Catholic church. The Program is committed to teaching Latin as a language. Instructors do not reduce Latin to mere matter for analysis, but make abundant use of experiential, communicative teaching strategies inspired by modern-language classrooms.
